citation: Hanley, P., Wilson, H., Holligan, B., & Elliott, L. (2020). Thinking, Doing, Talking Science: the effect on attainment and attitudes of a professional development programme to provide cognitively challenging primary science lessons. International Journal of Science Education, 42(15), 2554-2573. https://doi.org/10.1080/09500693.2020.1821931
report_number: DOI 10.1080/09500693.2020.1821931 (journal version of the EEF efficacy trial 'Thinking, Doing, Talking Science'; EEF/AstraZeneca/Science Oxford/Oxford Brookes; project also reported as Hanley, Slavin & Elliott 2016 EEF Oxford_Science.pdf). Distinct from Kitmitto et al. 2018 (the later EEF 'train-the-trainer' effectiveness trial).
design: Two-armed cluster RCT (assignment = School; schools matched into pairs at randomisation on pre-test, EAL, FSM and size, one of each pair to TDTS). 42 primary schools in Oxfordshire (England) randomised; 1 control school (38 pupils) withdrew -> 41 schools analysed (21 TDTS, 20 control). Pupils aged 9-10 (pre-test Year 4 Dec 2012/Jan 2013, post-test Year 5 June/July 2014). Subject = primary science. Intervention = Thinking, Doing, Talking Science (TDTS) teacher CPD: 2 teachers/school attend 5 training days over one academic year to deliver more cognitively challenging, practical and discussion-rich science lessons. Business-as-usual control (offered TDTS the following year). Efficacy trial. Original 1513 pupils; analysis restricted to 1264 pupils with both pre- and post-test (655 TDTS, 609 control; 16% pupil attrition, 2% school attrition).
problems: Open-access green copy used: author submitted/accepted manuscript on Oxford Brookes RADAR (CC-BY-NC-ND), confirmed via OpenAlex + Unpaywall (oa_status green). Page numbers here refer to the manuscript PDF (38 pp), not the journal pagination (2554-2573). Effect sizes are taken directly from Table 4 (p.33): pretest-adjusted HLM impact estimates standardised as Hedges (2007) cluster-randomised effect sizes (pupils nested in School nested in Pair; controlling for pre-test; CIs reported as estimate +/- 1.96 SE). These already account for clustering -> cluster_adjusted=true, pretest_adjusted=true. impact_se NOT printed; derived from the reported 95% CI as SE=(upper-lower)/(2*1.96); g_var=SE^2. The paper does NOT report the achieved/observed ICC; the only ICC given is the design-stage assumption ICC=0.10 (footnote 1, p.14, for the power calculation) -- recorded as icc with a note; not used to re-correct g (the g is already cluster-corrected). n_clusters=41 for the all-pupils contrast (41 schools in final analysis); subgroup contrasts draw on subsets of those 41 schools but the per-subgroup school count is not reported, so n_clusters=41 is recorded with a caveat (FSM was highly clustered: ~2/3 of FSM pupils in 11 schools, 4 schools with no FSM). The primary outcome test is researcher-administered but built from standardised assessment questions (NFER Russell & McGuigan 2001; reused from Bennett et al. 2019) -> labelled standardized_independent with a note (authors flag in limitations it was 'not a nationally standardised test', and was administered -- though not marked -- by staff aware of allocation). HEADLINE full-sample contrast = All pupils g=+0.22 (row_id 43). All other rows are non-randomised subgroups (gender, FSM, prior-attainment strata) -> outcome_role=subgroup, is_full_sample=false; provided for completeness, NOT for the main pooled estimate. Raw posttest means/SDs (Table 3, p.32) recorded alongside the model-based g. Single TPD arm vs single BAU control; only one science achievement outcome (no separate reading/maths transfer tests in this trial).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Thinking, Doing, Talking Science (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Primary science attainment test (40-min paper test, content + conceptual understanding + science inquiry process; questions from standardised assessments per Russell & McGuigan 2001 / NFER, reused from Bennett et al. 2019)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of Year 5, June/July 2014; immediate post-intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Taken directly from Table 4 (p.33, 'All pupils'): pretest-adjusted multilevel (HLM) impact standardised as a Hedges (2007) cluster-randomised effect size. g_se derived from reported 95% CI (0.11, 0.33): SE=(0.33-0.11)/(2*1.96)=0.0561; g_var=SE^2=0.00315. Consistent with raw-mean check (Table 3): (22.25-21.05)/sqrt(((655-1)*6.71^2+(609-1)*6.92^2)/(655+609-2))=1.20/6.81=0.176 unadjusted (lower than the pretest-adjusted 0.22, as expected since pre-test favoured control by 0.1 pts and adjustment increases precision).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.33 Table 4 (row 'All pupils'); narrative p.18; raw means p.32 Table 3
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY confirmatory full-sample outcome and the headline contrast for row_id 43. Science -> STEM per spec. Statistically significant, F(1, 36.50)=6.61, p=.014 (model); ES p<0.001; post-test 1.5 marks higher [95% CI 0.74, 2.25]; ~3 months' extra progress (Higgins et al. 2015 toolkit). n in model = 1264 (655 TDTS, 609 control). Pre-test means balanced: TDTS 24.2 (SD 6.8), control 24.3 (6.8); pre-post r=0.71. icc=0.10 is the design-stage assumption (footnote p.14); achieved ICC not reported; g is already cluster-corrected so no further correction needed. Test administered (not marked) by staff aware of allocation; built from standardised questions but not a nationally standardised test (authors' limitation). Note: a subsequent larger 'train-the-trainer' effectiveness trial (Kitmitto et al. 2018) did not replicate this overall effect.
